headline: Google's earnings miss wipes 12% off GOOGL overnight — the biggest story in your portfolio today — while the ASX closed slightly green despite the RBA's Cup Day rate hike looming.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: GOOGL cratered 12.3% last night after Alphabet's quarterly profit disappointed Wall Street. The Guardian reported the company lost roughly $500 billion in market value in a single session. Investors were hoping AI investments would be translating into bigger profits — they haven't yet. This is the big story of the day for your portfolio.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS fell another 4% today, continuing a brutal run. No specific news catalyst today — the lithium market remains deeply depressed as oversupply weighs on prices. PLS is down over 60% from your purchase price overall.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI dropped 2.8% today, dragged lower by the selloff in global tech and AI stocks following Google's earnings miss. The ETF holds a basket of AI-focused companies, so a bad night on NASDAQ flows directly into its price.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE slipped 1.2% today. Emerging markets came under pressure as the US dollar held firm and global risk sentiment softened slightly. No single country event stood out — broad-based weakness across Asia and EM.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS dipped 0.7% today, tracking last night's mild S&P 500 decline of 0.3%. The US market was weighed down by the NASDAQ tech selloff but the broader market held up reasonably well.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft barely moved last night, down just 0.16%, which tells you a lot. Azure cloud revenue came in at $33.2 billion — that's now being disclosed in dollars for the first time — and investors liked the AI growth story. MSFT held up well compared to Google's disaster.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two dipped about 1% last night with no major news. GTA 6 buzz continues — reports suggest the game's total landmass is nearly equal to GTA 4, GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2 combined, keeping long-term excitement alive.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG barely moved today, down 0.25%. As a diversified all-in-one fund it's naturally cushioned against single-stock shocks like Google's. Steady as she goes.

movers.name: DHHF ETF
movers.note: DHHF was essentially flat today, down just 0.22%. As a broad, diversified growth ETF it's doing exactly what it should — absorbing global volatility without big swings. Nothing to worry about here.

watch_today.title: GOOGL: Big drop, but is it a buying opportunity?
watch_today.detail: Google fell 12.3% last night after earnings disappointed — profits didn't grow as fast as Wall Street wanted despite heavy AI spending. You hold a small position (0.23 shares, current value ~A$91). The long-term thesis — Google's dominance in search, cloud, and AI — is still intact. Bloomberg called it a 'wobbly quarter, not a crisis.' If you have spare cash and believe in the 3-5 year story, this dip could be worth topping up. But it's not urgent — sit tight if you're not ready.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX: Down 60% — long-term thesis under pressure
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals fell another 4% today and is now down over 60% from your entry price. The lithium market is in a prolonged slump with global oversupply. There's no sign of a near-term recovery catalyst. For a long-term holder, the question is whether you still believe in the EV/battery storage decade-long story. If yes, sit tight — but this is one to watch closely. Only sell if you've genuinely lost conviction in the long-term case.

watch_today.title: RBA Cup Day rate hike almost certain — watch your mortgage
watch_today.detail: All four big banks and most economists are tipping the RBA will lift interest rates again on Melbourne Cup Day (Tuesday). That would be the fifth hike in this cycle. A sixth is now rated at around 50/50. Australia's inflation just came in at 4.3%, well above the RBA's target band. If you have a mortgage, Tuesday is the day to brace for another repayment increase.

watch_today.title: MSFT: Held firm after strong Azure results — hold confidently
watch_today.detail: Microsoft barely budged last night despite the broader tech selloff — a sign the market trusts its AI story. Azure revenue hit $33.2 billion and is accelerating. Your MSFT position is up nearly 20% overall. Nothing here changes the long-term case — sit tight.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX: Down on Google spillover — AI theme still long-term intact
watch_today.detail: Your Global X AI ETF dropped 2.8% today, mostly because it holds exposure to companies like Google and other AI-heavy tech stocks that sold off overnight. The AI investment theme over a 5-10 year horizon remains strong — Google's bad quarter doesn't change that. Hold and don't panic.

watch_today.title: Iran tensions + oil at $103 — watch energy prices
watch_today.detail: Crude oil jumped 1.5% last night to $103.48 a barrel as fears grow about potential US-Iran military conflict. A ship was reported on fire off Oman. VP JD Vance has sent a diplomatic letter to Tehran but Iran says the proposals are 'unacceptable.' If this escalates, oil could spike further — watch petrol prices and any ASX energy exposure.

world.summary: Two big storylines dominate global news today: the US is in the thick of midterm election tensions with Trump pushing hard on voter fraud claims, and the Middle East is on edge as US-Iran tensions escalate dangerously with diplomacy looking shaky.

stories.title: US midterms: Trump pushes voter fraud crackdown, courts push back
stories.why_it_matters: With US midterm elections approaching, the Trump administration is running an aggressive campaign claiming noncitizens are voting — pushing states to purge voter rolls and tighten certification rules. A federal judge has now ordered Trump officials to hand over details of demands sent to states, and is pressing for specifics. Separately, the administration is trying to block Senate election certification in Alaska. Courts are actively pushing back, but the fight is intensifying. This matters because the outcome of the midterms could shift control of Congress, affecting US economic and foreign policy for years.

stories.title: Iran war fears mount as diplomacy falters — ship on fire off Oman
stories.why_it_matters: VP JD Vance sent a diplomatic letter to Tehran in what may be a last-ditch effort to avoid renewed US-Iran military conflict. But Iran's response was cold — an official said the mediation proposals contain 'only unacceptable ideas.' Meanwhile, a ship was reported on fire off the coast of Oman, raising immediate fears of Iranian involvement. Oil prices jumped 1.5% to $103/barrel on the news. If conflict resumes, expect oil to spike sharply — that means higher petrol prices in Australia and more inflation pressure.

stories.title: Global economic outlook improving — but uncertainty clouds the picture
stories.why_it_matters: The global economic outlook is slowly improving heading into 2027, but major uncertainties remain — including Middle East conflict, US political instability, and stubbornly high inflation in developed economies like Australia. For investors, this means the recovery is real but fragile, and any geopolitical shock (like an Iran escalation) could quickly reverse gains.

stories.title: Fashion industry adapts to the Middle East's 'new reality'
stories.why_it_matters: Global luxury and fashion brands are recalibrating their strategies for the Middle East market amid regional conflict and shifting consumer patterns. The region has become a significant revenue source for major international brands, and how companies navigate political instability there will affect earnings. Worth watching if you have exposure to global consumer brands through your ETFs.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 nudged up 0.18% today to close at 8,908 — a solid result given global headwinds. Last night in the US, the NASDAQ took a big hit (down 1.38%) dragged by Google's earnings collapse, while the S&P 500 slipped a modest 0.3%. Oil jumped on Iran fears, gold dipped, and the Aussie dollar softened slightly.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Closed slightly higher today — the local market shook off overnight US tech weakness.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night's session — mild dip as Google's earnings miss weighed on sentiment.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Last night — hit hard by Google's 12% plunge. Tech-heavy index took the brunt of the pain.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Jumped on Iran escalation fears — a ship on fire off Oman spooked energy markets.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Pulled back slightly — still near record highs overall.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar slipped a touch — weak global sentiment and RBA uncertainty keeping it subdued.

politics.summary: Australian politics is dominated by one story: another RBA interest rate hike is almost certain on Melbourne Cup Day (Tuesday), with inflation at 4.3% and all four big banks tipping a rise. The government is also under fire over spending, has floated a ban on AI data centres in suburbs, and is defending a new EU trade deal.

stories.title: RBA near-certain to hike on Cup Day — sixth hike now a 50/50 bet
stories.why_it_matters: Australia's inflation rate hit 4.3% — well above the RBA's 2-3% target — and all four big banks (ANZ, CBA, NAB, Westpac) now expect the Reserve Bank to raise interest rates again on Melbourne Cup Day, Tuesday 3 November. That would be the fifth hike in this cycle. Markets are pricing a sixth hike as a coin-toss. Each 0.25% rate rise adds roughly $75/month to a $500,000 mortgage. A major bank has also warned that an Australian recession is now a 50/50 chance — a stark warning for households.

stories.title: Opposition demands audit of Albanese-Chalmers government spending
stories.why_it_matters: The Coalition is ramping up calls for a full audit of federal government spending under PM Albanese and Treasurer Chalmers, arguing the budget is blowing out and contributing to inflation. With Australia's inflation at 4.3% and recession risk rising, the government's spending record is becoming a major political battleground ahead of any future election.

stories.title: Labor to ban AI data centres from suburban areas
stories.why_it_matters: The Albanese government is planning to ban new AI data centres from being built in suburban Australia, citing power consumption concerns and the strain these facilities place on local electricity grids. As AI demand explodes globally, data centres are becoming enormous power users. This policy would push them to industrial zones or regional areas — affecting where tech companies can expand in Australia.

stories.title: Albanese defends $10bn EU trade deal amid Coalition criticism
stories.why_it_matters: PM Albanese is defending a new $10 billion trade deal with the European Union, but the Coalition is raising concerns about agricultural market access — worried Australian farmers may face new competition from European products — and climate-related clauses that could impose environmental conditions on Australian exporters. Trade deals of this size can take years to flow through to economic outcomes, but they shape which industries grow and which face pressure.

ai.summary: The AI world is buzzing with Google's launch of Gemini 4 Carbon — a new model focused specifically on cybersecurity — which is topping most AI benchmarks but isn't publicly available yet. Meanwhile, Google's earnings miss is raising questions about whether the massive AI spending by Big Tech is actually paying off.

stories.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Carbon — tops benchmarks, built for cybersecurity
stories.why_it_matters: Google has released Gemini 4 Carbon, a new AI model specifically designed to find and fix cybersecurity vulnerabilities in software code. It outperforms OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra and Anthropic's Claude on most benchmarks — but it's not available to the public yet. The name 'Carbon' reflects Google's naming convention for specialised versions of its flagship Gemini 4 model. In plain terms: this is an AI that can scan your code and spot security holes faster than any human team. CEO Sundar Pichai's launch rhetoric was bold enough that it reportedly rattled two rival AI companies.

stories.title: Microsoft's Azure revenue hits $33.2bn — AI cloud spending paying off
stories.why_it_matters: Microsoft disclosed for the first time that its Azure cloud division pulled in $33.2 billion in revenue last quarter — a number it had previously kept vague. Azure is accelerating, and Microsoft's AI integrations (like Copilot built on OpenAI's models) are being credited with winning new enterprise customers. This is why MSFT barely moved last night while Google got hammered — investors trust Microsoft's AI strategy is already delivering results.

stories.title: ARK Invest ranks Google, Anthropic, OpenAI as top AI intelligence leaders
stories.why_it_matters: ARK Invest — the high-profile tech investment firm run by Cathie Wood — has released its AI intelligence index, ranking Google (Gemini), Anthropic (Claude), and OpenAI (GPT) as the three leading frontier AI companies. For investors holding GOOG or GXAI.AX, this is a reminder that despite the bad earnings quarter, Google is still considered a top-tier AI player by serious analysts.

stories.title: Japan's cyberattack surge sparks debate over AI regulation
stories.why_it_matters: Japan has seen a dramatic surge in AI-assisted cyberattacks, and it's fuelling a serious political debate about how to regulate AI and tighten data security rules. Japan is one of the world's biggest tech economies, and new AI security laws there could set a precedent for the region — including Australia, which is also grappling with how to handle AI regulation.

sport.summary: NRL season is officially over — the Roosters won the 2026 Grand Final 19-18 over the Knights in a thriller at Accor Stadium. Post-season contract and retirement news is flowing thick and fast. In AFL, the 2027 fixture is out and Sydney is the big winner. And tennis legend Frank Sedgman, 99, is set to be honoured at the 2027 Australian Open.

stories.title: Roosters win 2026 NRL Grand Final 19-18 over the Knights
stories.why_it_matters: The 2026 NRL season ended in one of the tightest Grand Finals in recent memory — the Sydney Roosters defeated the Newcastle Knights 19-18 at Accor Stadium. A one-point margin means it almost certainly came down to the final play. The Knights would be gutted having come so close to their first title in years.

stories.title: NRL post-season: Rabbitohs forward retires, veteran eyes new Dragons deal
stories.why_it_matters: The post-Grand Final silly season is heating up. A Rabbitohs forward has announced retirement, while a veteran is seeking a new deal with the Dragons. Fox Sports also reports that Braith Anasta has revealed Adam Walker doesn't want to join one unnamed club — plus a 'big Bunnies twist' in the transfer market. The contract merry-go-round is just getting started.

stories.title: 2027 AFL fixture out — Sydney the big winner, St Kilda completely snubbed
stories.why_it_matters: The 2027 AFL fixture has been released and it's sparked immediate debate. Sydney Swans are the big winners — loaded with prime-time slots — while St Kilda has been completely shut out of Friday/Saturday night games in a major snub. Fox Sports graded every team and identified two clear losers in the scheduling. For fans, prime-time slots mean bigger crowds, more exposure, and ultimately more revenue for clubs.

stories.title: Frank Sedgman, 99, to be honoured at 2027 Australian Open
stories.why_it_matters: Australian tennis legend Frank Sedgman, who turns 100 next year, will be specially honoured at the 2027 Australian Open with his image on the match coin. Sedgman was the dominant Australian player of the early 1950s and a key figure in the golden era of Australian tennis. It's a wonderful tribute to a living piece of sporting history.
